This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.
SCCH-5 2.

The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 18.09.2022 at about 3.40 p.m. he had been travelling as a passenger in BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-01-F-4819, when the bus reached near Bapujinagar Bus Stand, the driver stopped the said bus on left side of the road, at that time, a Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-53-6617 being driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner came from behind without following traffic rules and regulations, without stopping the lorry suddenly steered towards extreme right, due to which back left portion of the body of the lorry knocked to back side window right portion of the BMTC bus, as a result of which, petitioner sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Penacle Hospital, after first aid, he was shifted to Victoria SCCH-5 Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as inpatient, for which he has spent more than Rs.80,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges etc.,
3.

At the time of the accident he was aged about 23 years, hale and healthy, working as Electrician,
thereby earning Rs.30,000/- p.m., due to this accident he is completely bed ridden, getting headache and giddiness often, cannot lift or carry weight, undergoing deep mental shock and pain and sufferings.

Out of this accident crime No.179/2022 is registered against the driver of the lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-53-6617 before the Byatarayanapura Traffic Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC.
Respondent No.1 is the R.C.Owner, respondent No.2 is insurer of the said lorry, they are jointly and severally liable to pay SCCH-5 compensation.
Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest.
4. On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has appeared and filed written statement and denied averments of the petition.
The petition suffers from non- joinder of proper and necessary parties.
Further denied age, occupation and income of the petitioner.

Further submitted that, he is owner of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-53-6617 and the driver of the said lorry had effective driving license bearing No.KA02 20020016124 and he was not responsible for the alleged accident.

Further submitted that, driver of the BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-01-F-4819 only drove the said bus in Ranganna vs Irfan.A on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151264886/
2 rash and negligent manner and dashed against the lorry and said lorry was insured with respondent No.2 under policy No.2315203493087802000 which is valid since SCCH-5 23.08.2022 to 22.08.2023.

5. Respondent No.2/insurer has filed written statement and denied petition averments.
There is no compliance of Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act.
Further denied the occurrence of the alleged accident involving the lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-53-6617.

Further denied age, occupation and income of the petitioner, occurrence of the accident, injuries sustained and treatment taken by the petitioner,
medical expenses incurred by him.
Further admitted issuance of insurance policy in respect of said lorry and if there is any liability to pay the compensation, it is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

6. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:
SCCH-5 ::ISSUES::
1. Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 18.09.2022 at about 3.40 p.m. when petitioner was a passenger in BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-01-F- 4819, near Bapujinagar Bus Stand, Bapujinagar, Bengaluru at that time, one Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-53-6617 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed behind the BMTC bus and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

7. In order to prove his case, Petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW-1, examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N. Orthopaedic Surgeon at SOADS is examined as PW-2 and marked 15 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.15 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, FDA, Rajajinagar SCCH-5 RTO by name Lakshmikanth is examined as RW-1 and marked documents as per Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.3.
The Legal Manager of respondent No.2 is examined as RW-2 and marked two documents as per Ex.R.4 and Ex.R.5 and closed her evidence.

3 9. Issue No.1:-
In order to prove his case, petitioner has deposed his evidence as PW-1, in his chief- examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts SCCH-5 averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated here.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of sketch is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.5,
copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.7, copy of Sec.133 notice is marked as Ex.P.8 and copy of reply notice is marked as Ex.P.9.
10.
Further to substantiate the petitioner case, he examined one Doctor as PW-2.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 and records those have marked i.e., FIR, complaint, spot mahazar,
sketch, IMV Report, charge sheet, Sec.133 notice and reply notice

corroborates the case of the petitioner about causing of the accident dated 18.09.2022 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
SCCH-5 11.
Per contra, FDA, Rajajinagar RTO by name Lakshmikanth is examined as RW-1 and he has exhibited authorization letter marked as Ex.R.1 and permit marked as Ex.R.2 and 3.
Further the Legal Manager of respondent No.2 Insurance Company is examined as RW-2.
Except above evidence, respondents have not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of the accident held on 18.09.2022 at about 3.40 p.m. while travelling in BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-01-F-4819 on Mysore Road, near Bapujinagar Bus Stand,
Bapujinagar, Bengaluru.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the SCCH-5 petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
12. The police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the lorry driver.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the above issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:-
As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained type III B open bicondylar fracture of the right distal humerus, for which he undertook treatment with ORIF with K wire.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.6, discharge card marked as Ex.P.10 issued by Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment SCCH-5 as indoor patient since 18.09.2022 to 26.09.2022.

Further he has furnished medical bills of Rs.17,103/-
marked as Ex.P. 11 and medical prescriptions marked as Ex.P.12.
14.
Ofcourse, PW-2 Dr.Nagaraj B.N. Orthopaedic Surgeon at SOADS Hospital is examined as PW-2.

To substantiate his evidence, he has exhibited clinical notes marked as Ex.P.14 and X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.15 and he has assessed total disability of the right arm at 38% and whole body physical disability at 12%.
In cross- examination he has categorically admitted that, he has not treated the petitioner, now the fracture is malunited and there is no implants in situ.

Further Ranganna vs Irfan.A on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151264886/

As per his case, he was working as Electrician thereby earning Rs.30,000/- p.m., to prove the said fact, there are no documents on record.

Under such circumstances, with reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner is taken at the rate of Rs.14,750/- p.m. so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss income during laid up period and also for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

18. Further admittedly petitioner has exhibited Ex.P.11 medical bills for Rs.17,103/-.
On perusal of the said bills it is clearly stated about spending of amount for his treatment is considered.

Further on perusal of Ex.P.6 SCCH-5 in which Doctor who have treated i.e., Dr.Usha B.R. has categorically stated that, petitioner has sustained grievous injury out of the accident caused on 18.09.2022.
So as per Ex.P.6 wound certificate, petitioner has sustained type 3 B open medial and lateral condyle fracture of humerus, which is grievous in nature.

During the course of arguments, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 Smt.GR argued that,
there is dispute with regard to liability of respondents in this case and lorry is not responsible for causing of the injuries to the petitioner and further as per the new Act, no pay and recovery principle is attracts to this case and petitioner himself has put his hand outside the window of the bus and there is no liability of respondent side, Doctor has given 12% disability and there is no avocation of the petitioner and prays to dismiss the petition.

21.

SCCH-5 23

. In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.2315 2034 9308 7802 000 which is valid for the period from 23.08.2022 to 22.08.2023, the alleged accident was occurred on 18.09.2022 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

Hence naturally liability of respondent No.1 shall go against respondent No.2, so Ranganna vs Irfan.A on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151264886/
6 that, respondent No.2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
24. Issue No.3:

For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
SCCH-5 The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,48,356/- (Rupees Four Lakhs Forty Eight Thousand Three Hundred Fifty Six Only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
